takeaway: Haematemesis in an alcoholic with hepatomegaly, spider naevi and palmar erythema suggests oesophageal varices from portal hypertension.

question.text: A 55-year-old writer has abdominal pain and haematemesis. He is ethanolic with hepatomegaly, spider naevi and palmar erythema. What is the diagnosis?
question.say: A fifty-five-year-old writer comes to A and E with abdominal pain and haematemesis. He is ethanolic, with hepatomegaly. He also has spider naevi and palmar erythema. What is the diagnosis?

lines.text: A 55-year-old writer is vomiting blood: haematemesis.
lines.say: This fifty-five-year-old writer is vomiting blood. That is haematemesis.

lines.text: He is ethanolic, with an enlarged liver.
lines.say: (sigh) He is ethanolic, with hepatomegaly, an enlarged liver.
He has spider naevi on his chest.

lines.text: And palmar erythema in his palm.
The veins in the lower oesophagus are dilated: oesophageal varices.
lines.say: The bleeding comes from oesophageal varices, dilated submucosal veins in the lower oesophagus.

lines.text: They are a consequence of portal hypertension.
lines.say: They are often a consequence of portal hypertension.

lines.text: Remember: a chronic liver patient who vomits blood has oesophageal varices.
lines.say: Remember: a patient with liver disease who vomits blood has oesophageal varices.
